title: Customizable Design Elements
description: Schema for the configurable portion of a design system: the color catalog, typeface and font definitions, semantic role definitions, and theme bindings. The active data file is referenced by the CUSTOMIZABLE_DESIGN_SYSTEM_ELEMENTS environment variable. Static guidance, fixed foundations, and architectural prose are not represented here.

$schema_version.description: Version of this schema the data file conforms to. Bumped when a breaking change is made.

Conventions.title: Conventions
Conventions.description: Machine-readable naming patterns. A code generator reads these to produce CSS variable names from data paths.

color_var_pattern.description: Pattern for color-token CSS variable names. {palette key} and {color key} are substituted from the data path.

typeface_var_pattern.description: Pattern for typeface CSS variable names. {typeface key} is the typeface identifier.

font_var_pattern.description: Pattern for semantic-font CSS variable names. {font key} is the font identifier (e.g., sans, serif, mono).

role_var_pattern.description: Pattern for role CSS variable names. {role key} is the role identifier.

spacing_var_pattern.description: Pattern for spacing-scale CSS variable names. {key} is the geometry.spacing identifier (e.g. 1, 2-5).

radius_var_pattern.description: Pattern for border-radius-scale CSS variable names. {key} is the geometry.radius identifier (e.g. sm, xl).

section_padding_var_pattern.description: Pattern for section-padding CSS variable names. {key} is the geometry.section_padding identifier (e.g. main, large).

container_var_pattern.description: Pattern for section-wrapper-width CSS variable names. {key} is the geometry.containers identifier (e.g. marketing-primary, editorial). A container is a section wrapper; its width is >= the page width.

column_var_pattern.description: Pattern for inner reading-column CSS variable names. {key} is the geometry.columns identifier (e.g. wide, reading). A reading column caps a single text block inside a page-width section; it is never a section wrapper.

component_size_var_pattern.description: Pattern for component-level geometry CSS variable names. {component} is the geometry.components key; {property} is the size/geometry property under it (e.g. topbar + logo-height -> --topbar-logo-height).

ease_var_pattern.description: Pattern for easing-curve CSS variable names. {key} is the motion.easing identifier (e.g. snap, in-out).

duration_var_pattern.description: Pattern for duration CSS variable names. {key} is the motion.duration identifier (e.g. 200, 600).

motion_pattern_var_pattern.description: Pattern for entrance-motion pattern parameter CSS variable names. {pattern} is the motion.patterns key; {property} is the parameter under it (e.g. reveal + stagger -> --reveal-stagger).

Color.title: Color
Color.description: A color value expressed in one or more color formats. At least one format is required.

oklch.description: OKLCH color space — perceptually uniform. Reserved for future use; current data is hex-based.

Func.title: Func
Func.description: A CSS function invocation. The object has exactly one property; its key is the function name (var, calc, clamp, color-mix, linear-gradient, etc.); its value is the function's argument expression as a string. Nested function calls are written inline inside the value string, not as nested objects. Property names cannot collide with Color's structural property names (hex, rgb, hsl, oklch, name) — that disambiguates Func from Color at validation time.

ColorValue.title: ColorValue
ColorValue.description: A color slot: either a literal Color or a Func reference (e.g., {var: '--color-blue-750'}).

PaletteType.description: Ramp = ordered stepwise progression (typically numeric keys 050, 100, ... 950). Discrete = unordered named colors (e.g., oat, peach, fig). The tag is informational; downstream tooling decides what to do with it.

Palette.title: Palette
Palette.description: A named group of colors. Keys in `colors` become path segments in the generated CSS variable name (see $conventions.colorVarPattern).

description.description: Optional one-sentence statement of what the palette IS / is for — never its contents, consumers, or history. Enforced by lint-elements.py DESCRIPTIONS.

colors.description: Map of color identifier to color value. Identifier becomes the {color key} segment of the CSS variable name. For Ramp palettes, keys should be zero-padded numeric strings (050, 100, ..., 950); for Discrete palettes, kebab-case names.

examples.description: Aliases — every value is a reference to another color.

ColorCatalog.title: ColorCatalog
ColorCatalog.description: The complete set of raw color values. Primitives and aliases. Roles and themes reference values from here.

common_colors.description: Catalog-wide foundational colors that don't belong to any single palette (typically white and black).

palettes.description: Map of palette identifier to palette. Palette identifier becomes the {palette key} segment of the generated CSS variable name.

FontAxisRange.title: FontAxisRange
FontAxisRange.description: Continuous range for a variable-font axis (e.g., weight 300..900, optical-size 7..72).

Typeface.title: Typeface
Typeface.description: An individual typeface. Records the typeface's intrinsic attributes only (name and axes). Hosting paths, source URLs, and build-time configuration are not part of this object.

name.description: Display name of the typeface (e.g., 'Host Grotesk').

type.description: Whether the typeface is a single-instance static face or a multi-axis variable font.

weights.description: Available weight axis. Either an enumerated list (static face) or a min/max range (variable font weight axis).

italic.description: Whether the typeface provides an italic style or axis.

Typefaces.title: Typefaces
Typefaces.description: Map of typeface identifier to typeface definition. The identifier becomes the {typeface key} segment of the generated CSS variable name (see $conventions.typeface_var_pattern).

Font.title: Font
Font.description: A semantic font entry. Assigns a typeface to a generic category and carries the category-specific fallback chain.

typeface.description: Reference to a typeface in the typefaces catalog (e.g., { var: '--typeface-host-grotesk' }).

fallback.description: CSS font-family fallback chain (comma-separated). Should end in the generic family (sans-serif, serif, monospace) appropriate to the category.

Fonts.title: Fonts
Fonts.description: Map of font identifier to font definition. The identifier becomes the {font key} segment of the generated CSS variable name (see $conventions.font_var_pattern).

RoleType.description: The kind of value that fills this role. Determines which ValueType is valid in theme bindings.

RoleScope.description: semantic = general role any component may consume (e.g., --surface-primary). component = role tied to a specific component (e.g., --button-primary-bg).

Role.title: Role
Role.description: A named placeholder in the semantic or component layer. Filled by a theme; consumed by a component via var().

description.description: One sentence stating what this role IS / is for (what paints, where, why) — never its current contents, consumers, or history. Enforced by lint-elements.py DESCRIPTIONS.

component.description: If scope is 'component', the component this role belongs to (e.g., 'button-primary', 'switch'). Optional for semantic roles.

family.description: Optional grouping for related roles (e.g., 'surface', 'text', 'border'). Roles in the same family share lightness ranking or similar semantics.

required.description: Must every theme bind this role? If false, the role only needs binding in themes that host the component it serves.

from_palette.description: Palette constraint. Declares that any theme binding for this role MUST resolve — following the var() alias chain — into one of the named palettes in color_catalog.palettes. This is how a role says 'only choose a color from the panels palette.' A string names a single palette; an array names several (a binding satisfies the constraint if it lands in any one of them). The field is recorded here so it is a known, documented property; the resolve-and-check enforcement is performed by the elements linter, because JSON Schema cannot follow a var() reference to its target palette. Components never name a color — they consume this role, and this constraint bounds what the theme may put in it.

fallback.description: Fallback value if no theme binds this role. Used when var() resolves to nothing. Most roles should have a fallback so an unwrapped section doesn't paint invisibly.

constraints.description: Free-form constraints not captured by the schema (e.g., 'must provide ≥7:1 contrast against text-primary'). Informational; not enforced.

examples.description: Page ground. Default background of any section that doesn't override.
Primary-action button fill. Inverts with mode.

Roles.title: Roles
Roles.description: Map of role identifier to role definition. The identifier becomes the {role key} segment of the generated CSS variable name (see $conventions.role_var_pattern).

ThemeMode.title: ThemeMode
ThemeMode.description: A theme's bindings for one mode (light or dark). Each binding maps a role identifier to either a literal value or a Func reference to a color token.

description.description: Optional note describing this mode's character (e.g., 'Body text inverts to cool light against the blue ground').

bindings.description: Map of role identifier to the value it resolves to in this (theme, mode) pair.

Theme.title: Theme
Theme.description: A named theme — either a concrete theme that declares its own role bindings (ConcreteTheme) or an alias that mirrors another concrete theme (AliasTheme). Exactly one of the two forms applies to any given theme entry.

ConcreteTheme.title: ConcreteTheme
ConcreteTheme.description: A named theme that declares its own role bindings. A theme that changes appearance on light/dark mode flip declares BOTH a 'light' and a 'dark' mode, each binding every role. A theme that does NOT change between modes declares only its active mode (its single 'light' mode — which for an inherently-dark theme still holds dark swatches); the redundant mode is retained in the source data file as a fully-commented-out template that a maintainer can uncomment and edit to make the theme diverge in that mode. An absent mode therefore means 'identical to the theme's active mode'.

description.description: What this theme is for, where it's used, what character it carries (e.g., 'Principal warm light theme — default page ground').

modes.description: Map of mode name to ThemeMode. Standard modes are 'light' and 'dark'. The schema doesn't enforce which modes exist; a linter does. A theme that doesn't change between modes legitimately defines only its active mode here; the other mode is carried as a commented-out template in the source file and is therefore absent from the parsed data.

AliasTheme.title: AliasTheme
AliasTheme.description: A theme with no bindings of its own; it mirrors a concrete theme. The generator emits the alias's selector grouped with the target theme's, so the alias shares 100% of the target's generated rules in every mode — base bindings plus any dark-mode override. The alias→target mapping lives here in data; the generator must not hardcode it.

alias.description: Key of the concrete theme this alias mirrors. Must name a theme defined in this same `themes` map that is itself concrete — aliases do not chain. The target's existence and concreteness are enforced by the elements linter (JSON Schema cannot cross-reference sibling keys).

description.description: What this alias is for (e.g., 'Editorial and legal pages — a semantic name for the default warm-light ground').

Themes.title: Themes
Themes.description: Map of theme class name (e.g., 'default', 'clarity', 'deep') to theme definition. Class names are bare role-based identifiers with no methodology prefix. A value is either a concrete theme (declares `modes`) or an alias (declares `alias`).

GeometryToken.title: GeometryToken
GeometryToken.description: A single configurable geometry value emitted as one CSS custom property. `value` is the CSS the generator emits verbatim — a literal length ('84px'), a clamp() interpolation, a keyword, or a var() reference to another geometry token ('var(--topbar-height)'). The generator wraps the value in the §11.1 clamp form only when the data already expresses it; it does not invent interpolation.

value.description: The CSS value emitted for this token (literal, clamp(), keyword, or var() reference).

description.description: Optional human-readable note on what this geometry value is for.

mobile_floor.title: MobileFloor
mobile_floor.description: Optional narrow-viewport override. The generator re-declares this token at :root inside `@media (max-width: <max_width>)` so every consumer of the token picks up the floor without per-component media queries (mirrors the §11.3 --section-pad-main pattern).

value.description: The token value at and below the breakpoint (e.g. '56px').

examples.description: Logo glyph height — tracks the bar.

GeometryScale.title: GeometryScale
GeometryScale.description: A named scale: map of scale-step key to GeometryToken. The key becomes the {key} segment of the scale's var pattern (e.g. spacing key '2-5' -> --sp-2-5).

GeometryComponent.title: GeometryComponent
GeometryComponent.description: Per-component sizing/geometry: map of property name to GeometryToken. {property} becomes the second segment of component_size_var_pattern (e.g. topbar + logo-height -> --topbar-logo-height). This is how the DESIGN SYSTEM, not the page, owns a component's dimensions.

Geometry.title: Geometry
Geometry.description: The configurable geometry element set — page-, surface-, and component-level sizing, spacing, and geometry. A first-class peer to color and motion. The generator emits each entry as a CSS custom property in tokens.css and the component classes in components.css consume them, so component sizing lives in the design system and never has to be re-invented in a page's style block.

spacing.description: The shared spacing scale (emitted via spacing_var_pattern, default --sp-{key}).

radius.description: The border-radius scale (emitted via radius_var_pattern, default --radius-{key}).

section_padding.description: The section-padding scale (emitted via section_padding_var_pattern, default --section-pad-{key}).

containers.description: Section-wrapper widths per surface class (emitted via container_var_pattern, default --container-{key}). A section wrapper's width is >= the page width; a surface chooses a container token instead of hardcoding a max-width in the page. Inner reading columns live in `columns`, not here.

columns.description: Inner reading-column widths (emitted via column_var_pattern, default --column-{key}). A reading column caps a SINGLE text block or one card inside a page-width section; it is never used as the section wrapper. Distinct from `containers` (section-wrapper widths, >= page width).

components.title: GeometryComponents
components.description: Map of component key (matching a components.md family, e.g. 'topbar') to its GeometryComponent sizing block.

MotionToken.title: MotionToken
MotionToken.description: A single configurable motion value emitted as one CSS custom property: an easing curve ('cubic-bezier(...)'), a duration ('200ms', '0.75s'), or an entrance-pattern parameter (a length, time, or var() reference such as 'var(--ease-out-quart)').

value.description: The CSS value emitted for this token.

description.description: Optional note on what this motion value drives.

MotionTokenSet.title: MotionTokenSet
MotionTokenSet.description: A named set of motion tokens: map of key to MotionToken (e.g. easing key 'in-out' -> --ease-in-out, duration key '200' -> --duration-200).

MotionPattern.title: MotionPattern
MotionPattern.description: Parameters for one entrance-motion pattern (reveal, card-stagger, fade, fade-up): map of parameter name to MotionToken. {property} becomes the second segment of motion_pattern_var_pattern (e.g. reveal + stagger -> --reveal-stagger). The generator emits these parameters as tokens AND emits the matching @keyframes + pattern class that consumes them — animating in the base rule and disabling only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

Motion.title: Motion
Motion.description: The configurable motion element set — easing curves, durations, and entrance-pattern parameters. A first-class peer to color and geometry. The generator emits the tokens into tokens.css AND emits the reveal/stagger/fade keyframes and pattern classes into the generated CSS so motion lives in the design system; composers apply the pattern classes with reduced-motion gating instead of authoring entrance keyframes per page.

easing.description: Named easing curves (emitted via ease_var_pattern, default --ease-{key}).

patterns.title: MotionPatterns
patterns.description: Map of entrance-pattern name (reveal, card-stagger, content-fade, content-fade-up) to its MotionPattern parameter block.

Assets.title: Assets
Assets.description: Optional brand-asset declarations. Currently carries the logo rendering mode.

logo.title: LogoAsset
logo.description: How the brand logo is rendered. Default: a single currentColor glyph that inherits --text-primary and recolors with the theme. A multi-color brand mark MAY instead declare a light/dark image pair — the one supported exception to the single-glyph rule (compliance.md §23 #15).

light.description: Path or URL to the logo asset shown on light grounds.

dark.description: Path or URL to the logo asset shown on dark grounds.

alt.description: Accessible alt text for the logo image.
